**GFT** is seeking a **Project Environmental Scientist** to join our growing Environmental Practice! This role follows a hybrid work model, requiring regular attendance at either our **Berkeley, CA or Roseville, CA** offices.  

GFT’s Environmental team delivers integrated planning, permitting, and compliance solutions that support infrastructure development across North America. With more than 140 professionals in 22 offices, the team guides clients through NEPA and permitting processes, ecological and regulatory assessments, and environmental remediation efforts. Their expertise spans transportation, power, water, and facilities markets — working alongside agencies at federal, state, and local levels. From stream restoration to complex regulatory requirements and advance critical infrastructure projects. **What you’ll be challenged to do:**
This is an excellent career opportunity for an experienced, motivated Project Environmental Scientist who is ready to take the next step in their career. We are looking for someone how combines strong technical permitting expertise – a professional that enjoys doing the work, working directly with clients and regulatory agencies and helping to building a growing environmental practice.
The successful candidate will have strong working knowledge of California and federal environmental permitting requirements, particularly as they apply to transportation, water and power projects. This individual will lead and prepare permit applications and technical documentation, coordinate with regulatory agencies, manage permitting assignments and support projects through planning and through design and construction. **In this capacity, the successful candidate will be responsible for the following:*** Lead and support natural resource analysis and environmental permitting for transportation, water, and other infrastructure projects throughout California.
* Develop permitting strategies and identify federal, state, and local regulatory requirements during project planning, CEQA/NEPA and design.
* Prepare and manage permit applications and supporting technical documentation, including Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, California Fish and Game Code Section 1600 Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements, and other applicable federal, state, and local permits and approvals.
* Coordinate directly with regulatory agencies, including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Boards, California Department of Fish and Wildlife, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, NOAA Fisheries, and other agencies as appropriate.
* Conduct wetland delineations, jurisdictional assessments, biological field studies, and other technical investigations necessary to support project permitting as well as CEQA/NEPA analysis.
* Author and review technical reports, CEQA/NEPA analysis, permit applications, environmental commitments, mitigation plans, and related environmental deliverables.
* Work closely with engineering and design teams to identify natural resource and permitting constraints, develop practical avoidance and minimization measures, and incorporate environmental requirements into project design and construction.
* Support environmental compliance during construction, including implementation and tracking of permit conditions and mitigation commitments.
* Manage environmental permitting assignments, including scope, schedule, budget, staffing, deliverables, and client communications.
* Contribute to and increasingly lead environmental components of proposals, interviews, scopes of work, and cost estimates.
* Contribute to the continued development of GFT’s California Environmental Practice.

* Approximately 5\-8 years of progressively responsible experience, with significant experience delivering natural resources and permitting services for infrastructure projects.
* Demonstrated experience preparing and managing environmental permits for projects in California.
* Strong working knowledge of applicable federal and California environmental regulations.
* Experience working with and developing relationships with regulatory agencies such as USACE, CDFW, RWQCB, USFWA and/or NOAA Fisheries.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Self\-starter, able to complete tasks with minimal supervision and direction.
* Willingness to travel and execute work in a variety of settings and environmental conditions (heat, cold, rain, etc.).
* Demonstrated leadership and interpersonal skills to work effectively with others and achieve results.
* Demonstrated agility working with multi\-disciplined infrastructure projects.
* Demonstrated professional judgment, consistency, strong attention to detail, and background of high\-quality work products.
* Ability to prepare and deliver presentations and lead meetings, when needed.
* An entrepreneurial mindset and interest in helping grow a developing California environmental practice.

**What we prefer you bring:*** A Master’s degree in environmental science, biology, ecology or a closely related field.
* Established relationships with California transportation agencies, water agencies, municipalities, regulatory agencies, or other infrastructure clients.
* Experience with Caltrans, local transportation agencies, passenger rail/transit agencies, water districts, utilities, or similar California public\-sector clients.
* GIS experience.
* Relevant professional certifications or specialized permitting/natural\-resource credentials.

### **Location: California**


Aspen Environmental Group is seeking an experienced and motivated Air Quality Specialist to support projects focused primarily on CEQA/NEPA analysis, air quality impact modeling, and greenhouse gas emissions inventory evaluations. The Air Quality Specialist will work as part of a multidisciplinary environmental team and collaborate with other recognized experts.


Aspen’s Air Quality \& Climate Services group supports environmental compliance projects, including Air Quality Impact Analysis, Compliance Audit Evaluations, and Climate Change Analysis. Learn more about our Air Quality \& Climate Services at: https://www.aspeneg.com/service/air\-quality\-climate\-services

#### **Required Education and Experience**

* B.S. degree in Engineering (Environmental, Civil, Chemical, or Mechanical) or Science (Environmental, Atmospheric, Meteorological, Chemistry, Toxicology, or Data Science) required; M.S. and/or P.E. a plus.
* Minimum of 5 to 8 years of direct consulting, public agency, or industry experience in air quality\-related aspects of CEQA/NEPA services.

#### **Key Responsibilities**

* Write environmental impact analyses, assess regulatory compliance, and perform regulatory applicability evaluations.
* Write evaluations of complex air quality impact analyses, compliance, and permitting situations.
* Perform multiple tasks within scope, budget, and schedule expectations and ensure quality standards on project deliverables.
* Communicate environmental standards to management and/or clients.
* Interact and maintain successful relationships with clients, in\-house project managers and staff, and subcontractors.
* Work independently and with teams to complete assignments.
* Deliver assignments on time and within the allotted budget.
* Engage in business development efforts.

#### **Qualifications for Success**

* Subject matter expertise in air pollution principles, air quality impact analysis methodologies, greenhouse gas emissions inventory development and management strategies, and California policies and regulatory programs of local air districts and the state.
* Actively stays informed regarding the changing regulatory landscape in California.
* Experience with AERMOD dispersion modeling and related software for ambient impact evaluation and health risk assessment.
* Ability to work independently while maintaining a strong focus on environmental protection, health, safety, quality, budget, and schedule.
* Highly developed organizational skills, with attention to both the big picture and detail, to meet competing deadlines and demands.
* Excellent technical writing and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to succeed in a fast\-paced consulting environment, handle multiple project assignments, and meet strict deadlines.
* Success in new business development preferred.
* Proficiency in Excel, Word, and basic computer skills required.

#### **Compensation**


The pay range for this role is $97,000 \- $130,000 commensurate with experience.

#### **To Apply**


Please submit a letter of interest, resume, references, and a recent writing sample in which the candidate was the sole author to humanresources@aspeneg.com. The subject line must state, “Air Quality Specialist – \[NAME].”

This position will play a critical role in the coordination of field crews conducting nutria surveys and trapping across the southern portion of the nutria infestation. * Role with genuine project ownership \& technical responsibility
* Company Vehicle, competitive salary, overtime
* Strong career development with the backing of global Kiwa group


  

Kiwa ELS is a customer\-focused, results\-driven risk management consultancy with offices in Brisbane and Sydney. We deliver hazardous materials, occupational hygiene, environmental and risk management consulting services to clients across Australia.  

  

As part of the Kiwa Group—a global leader in testing, inspection and certification with more than 12,000 professionals across 35\+ countries—we offer the backing of an international organisation while maintaining a strong local presence.  

  

Working alongside our NATA\-accredited laboratory, our Hazardous Materials team provides asbestos, mould and hazardous materials management, assessment and advisory services to an established client base across the construction, facilities management, transport, insurance and government sectors.  

  

Due to continued growth, we are seeking a full\-time Senior Hazardous Materials Consultant to join our Brisbane\-based team.  

  

Approximately 60% of your time will be spent on site across Southeast Queensland, undertaking hazardous materials and occupational hygiene work. The remaining 40% will be office\-based and focused on technical reporting, project management, proposals, quality assurance and supporting the development of other consultants. Occasional travel to regional locations and interstate may also be required.  

  

**What you will be doing**  

* Conduct asbestos, mould and hazardous materials surveys across industrial, commercial and residential properties.
* Undertake clearance inspections and airborne asbestos fibre monitoring associated with asbestos removal work.
* Complete contamination and post\-remediation verification assessments for asbestos, mould, moisture and other contaminants.
* Conduct occupational hygiene surveys and monitoring
* Manage projects, including developing scopes of work, preparing fee proposals, coordinating resources and ensuring project objectives and deadlines are achieved.
* Produce clear, accurate hazardous materials and occupational hygiene reports.
* Undertake technical review and quality assurance of reports prepared by other consultants.
* Provide technical guidance, training and mentoring to less experienced consultants.
* Liaise with clients and stakeholders to understand project requirements and provide practical technical advice.
* Perform laboratory analysis, including fibre counting for airborne asbestos, where required.
* Conduct respirator face fit testing when required.
* Ensure client deliverables are completed accurately and within agreed timeframes.
* Quality Assurance support when required

**Why work with us?**  

* Company vehicle provided.
* Competitive salary \& overtime based on your experience.
* Senior position with genuine project ownership and technical responsibility.
* Opportunity to mentor and support the development of other consultants.
* Ongoing training and career development opportunities.
* Kiwa Rewards, including discounts on shopping, travel, insurance and more.
* Access to our Employee Assistance Program.
* Supportive local team with the backing of a global organisation.


  

**Experience and qualifications**  

* 3\+ years’ experience in hazardous materials consulting, occupational hygiene or a closely related field.
* A current LAA licence is essential.
* A current Australian driver’s licence is essential.
* Science, environmental or hazardous materials qualifications, including relevant P\-Certs, are desirable.
* Professional membership with AIOH, FAMANZ or a similar industry body will be highly regarded.
* Demonstrated experience preparing and reviewing technical reports.
* Experience managing projects, developing scopes and preparing fee proposals will be highly regarded.

**About you**  

* Strong asbestos and/or Occ Hygiene background \- Technically strong and confident providing advice to clients, contractors and other consultants.
* Comfortable balancing hands\-on fieldwork with reporting, project management and technical review.
* Well organised and capable of managing multiple projects, priorities and deadlines.
* Able to communicate clearly and professionally with a broad range of stakeholders.
* Confident mentoring and providing constructive technical feedback to other consultants.
* Practical, safety\-focused and detail\-oriented.
* Able to work independently while contributing positively to the wider team.

If you are an experienced hazardous materials professional looking for a senior role that combines fieldwork, project ownership and technical leadership, apply now to join the Kiwa ELS team.
